stem:
Aditya places ice cubes in a steel bowl on the table. The ice melts into water. He wants evidence to make sense of the changes.

He considers four possible records:
1  the temperature of the water in the bowl every two minutes
2  the brand name printed on the steel bowl
3  whether the ice cubes had fully melted after ten minutes
4  how many times he heard a drip into the bowl

parts.text: Which set could count as evidence of what happened during the experiment?
Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Temperatures, melt outcomes, and drip counts are observations from the melting; the brand name on the bowl is not evidence of those changes.

teacher.key_rationale: Evidence is observed or measured during melting: temperatures, yes/no melt status, and drip counts. A printed brand name is not experimental evidence of the change.
